title: Optimistic KV-prefetch proxy and partial-response degrade for high-saturation downstreams
creator: Ava Martinez
description: We need a middleware proxy layer that reduces tail latency and preserves SLOs during downstream saturation by (1) performing optimistic prefetches for common key prefixes, (2) returning partial but useful responses when backends are degraded, and (3) operating with hygienic circuit-breaker probes and per-tenant soft quotas. This ticket scopes a pragmatic implementation for Redis-backed KV reads and a compatible pattern for Kafka fanout-to-KV reads. The proxy sits in front of existing connection pools and implements a lightweight response composition protocol so callers can distinguish full vs partial results.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end path: under sustained 3x baseline QPS to Redis read tier, p50 latency increase < 1.2x and p95 latency stays within SLO target; p99 improvement of at least 10% vs baseline without proxy

When Redis read-pool starts shedding connections, 90% of requests receive a partial response that includes a validity flag and covered-key ranges; callers can fall back to cached results or UI placeholders
Circuit-breaker engages for a given downstream shard after N consecutive probe failures and auto-recovers after health probes succeed for M intervals
Per-tenant soft quotas allow emergency admission (low-fidelity responses) for P0 tenants while throttling P3 tenants
Unit/integration tests cover optimistic-prefetch hit/miss, partial-response composition, and circuit breaker transitions
Feature gated behind a config flag and rollout toggles; no user-facing change unless flag enabled
implementation_steps: Design proxy protocol: define partial-response JSON envelope with fields {status, covered_keys, timestamp, sources} and backward-compatible header for SDKs
Implement optimistic-prefetch: maintain short-term LRU of recently-read key prefixes and issue async prefetches into proxy local cache before synchronous fetch
Integrate with existing connection pool: add a non-blocking admission path that attempts to borrow a connection and, on timeout, returns partial response rather than blocking callers
Circuit breaker: implement probe-based CB that tracks success latency distribution per shard and opens after configurable error/latency thresholds
Per-tenant token banking: attach lightweight admission tokens per request to prioritize P0/P1 tenants and allow emergency partial responses
Observability hooks: emit spans for prefetch hits/misses, CB state transitions, admission outcomes, and covered key ranges
Add feature flag and runtime knobs (prefetch window, prefetch concurrency, CB thresholds, partial response policy) exposed in Console
Write unit and integration tests; run chaos tests simulating Redis slow responses and connection exhaustion
Document behavior in engineering runbook and SDK notes; prepare rollout checklist
monitoring: Dashboard: proxy.p50/p95/p99, redis.borrow_time, prefetch_hit_ratio, partial_response_rate, cb_open_count
Alerts: partial_response_rate > 5% sustained for 10m (warning), >15% sustained for 5m (critical)
CB Alert: shard-specific CB open duration > 2m
SLO guard: overall request success-rate (full responses) falls below 99.0% for 30m
rollout_plan: Stage 1: internal canary (5% traffic) in staging region, validate metrics and rollback criteria
Stage 2: low-risk tenants opt-in in us-west with feature flag for 48h; verify prefetch hit ratios and CB behavior
Stage 3: progressive ramp to 50% region traffic with dynamic knobs enabled; monitor partial_response_rate and tail latency
Stage 4: full roll in the region if SLOs stable for 72h; then enable in additional regions with region-aware CB thresholds
Rollback criteria: sustained p99 increase > 20% or partial_response_rate > 25% not explained by traffic shift
risks: Over-aggressive prefetch can amplify load on Redis; mitigate with backpressure and prefetch concurrency cap
Partial responses may complicate client logic; require clear SDK changes and fallbacks
Incorrect CB thresholds could flip open too often under transient blips; need conservative default and automatic annealing
Per-tenant token banking state adds memory overhead; ensure bounded memory and eviction policy
metrics: prefetch_hit_ratio (goal: >= 35% after warmup for targeted keyspaces)
redis.borrow_time.p95 (reduce by >=10% vs baseline after rollout)
test_plan: Unit tests for proxy envelope serialization and partial response semantics
Integration tests against local Redis and embedded Kafka fanout simulating slow shards
Chaos: inject packet delays and connection drops to validate CB and prefetch backoff
Load test: 3x baseline sustained for 30 minutes to validate admission and partial response behavior
Client SDK tests to ensure callers can detect partial responses and surface fallback UI
notes: Reviewers: Leah Chen (runtime), Mateo Alvarez (platform), Priya Singh (observability)
